title: VehicleListResponse
description: Envelope returned by GET /api/vehicles. Wraps an array of VehicleSummary rows under the `items` key. Pagination fields are reserved per rest-api.md §7.0 and intentionally absent in v1. The envelope itself is part of the wire contract: consumers MUST NOT strip it silently.

items.description: Per-vehicle summary rows for vehicles the caller has access to. Order is server-defined (currently ORDER BY Vehicle.createdAt ASC in the telemetry list query). An empty array means the caller has no vehicles (or is a v1 viewer-tier caller — see rest-api.md §7.0 RBAC v1 implementation note).

VehicleSummary.title: VehicleSummary
VehicleSummary.description: Lean per-vehicle row returned by GET /api/vehicles. A list-view projection of VehicleState containing only the fields the catalog UI needs (identity, model/year/color, status, charge headline, last-updated). No GPS, no navigation, no climate, no encrypted-at-rest fields. Mirrors the Go `vehicleSummary` struct in telemetry/internal/telemetry/vehicles_list_handler.go and the `VehicleSummary` shape in telemetry/specs/rest.openapi.yaml. Use VehicleState for the full snapshot/WebSocket payload; use VehicleSummary for list endpoints.

vehicleId.description: Opaque database identifier (cuid). NOT the VIN. All SDK API calls use this ID (FR-4.2). Matches VehicleState.vehicleId.

name.description: User-assigned vehicle name from DB Vehicle.name. Matches VehicleState.name.

model.description: Vehicle model (e.g., 'Model 3', 'Model Y'). Sourced from DB Vehicle.model. Matches VehicleState.model. POPULATED FOR EVERY CAR SINCE MYR-507 (contracts v0.31.0) — the field, the type and the masks are all unchanged; only the PROVENANCE is new, exactly as MYR-320 did for the sibling `color`. Until then this column was filled only for vehicles linked through the Prisma web flow: the Go server's own provisioning INSERT seeded it with the empty placeholder '' and no writer, Go or Prisma, ever filled it in, so a car linked through the Go path reported an EMPTY MODEL forever. It is now derived from position 4 of the VIN (the model line) at link time and backfilled on the non-waking refresh for cars already in the table. FILL-IF-EMPTY, NEVER OVERWRITE: a row whose model was already populated keeps it, because the Prisma flow writes a richer value for some cars ('Model 3 Performance') than a VIN position can encode ('Model 3'). EMPTY-STRING CONVENTION unchanged: the key is ALWAYS present, and '' means 'not determined' — a VIN whose model code this server does not recognise, which it will never guess at. Consumers MUST keep a fallback label for '' and MUST NOT render an empty model fragment in a descriptor.

year.description: Model year. Sourced from DB Vehicle.year. Matches VehicleState.year. POPULATED FOR EVERY CAR SINCE MYR-507 (contracts v0.31.0) — same story, same placeholder problem and same fix as the sibling `model` above, which see. Derived from position 10 of the VIN (the ISO 3779 model-year code); Tesla's Fleet API carries no model year at ANY path, on vehicle_data or elsewhere, so the VIN is the platform's only source of one. FILL-IF-EMPTY, NEVER OVERWRITE. ZERO-VALUE CONVENTION: the key is ALWAYS present, and 0 means 'not determined' — a VIN whose year code falls outside the 2010-2030 letter window this server recognises. 0 is NEVER a real model year: consumers MUST treat it exactly as they treat an empty `model`, dropping the fragment from a descriptor rather than rendering 'Year 0'.

trimLabel.description: The DISPLAY-READY trim of this vehicle — 'Plaid', 'Performance', 'Long Range' (MYR-507, contracts v0.31.0). THE SAME VALUE, THE SAME COLUMN AND THE SAME SEMANTICS as VehicleState.trimLabel (rest-api.md §7.1, MYR-320): the snapshot does not derive this, it reads it, and the catalog now reads the same column, so the two surfaces cannot name one car two different things. Source: `trim_label` on the Go-owned `go_vehicle_control_state` side table (migration 0018), written from Tesla REST `vehicle_data.vehicle_config.performance_package` on the non-waking connectivity-edge / periodic in-service read. CARRIED ON THE CATALOG AS WELL AS THE SNAPSHOT ON PURPOSE, and for a consumer the snapshot cannot serve: a VIEWER never fetches a /snapshot, so the catalog row is the ONLY surface on which a shared car can say what it is. Without it a rider's vehicle descriptor degraded to the raw colour token — a Live Activity subline reading 'UltraRed', and a review-sheet row whose model slot rendered the bare make 'Tesla'. Together with the siblings `year`, `model` and `color` this row now carries everything a '2026 Model X Plaid · Ultra Red' descriptor needs. NOT THE RAW BADGE CODE: VehicleState.trim carries Tesla's `trim_badging` ('p74d'), which is explicitly NOT display-safe and is deliberately absent from the catalog under BOTH roles. Only the label may be rendered. OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: an ABSENT key means a server predating v0.31.0 and MUST be read exactly like null. NULL IS NOT THE EMPTY STRING and is the ordinary state for a car Tesla has not yet been asked about: it means 'no trim known', and a descriptor builder MUST drop the fragment entirely rather than emit a stray separator. RBAC: BOTH roles — an equipment fact of exactly the tier of its identity siblings `model`/`year`/`color`, all of which have been in both allow-lists since v1, and all of which are legible through a windshield from the kerb (the badge on the boot lid IS the trim). There is nothing here for masking to protect. Delivery: REST-READ-TIME ONLY; a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries it, so it refreshes on the next list fetch or /snapshot.

color.description: Vehicle exterior color. Sourced from DB Vehicle.color. Matches VehicleState.color.

location.description: Where this vehicle was last known to be (MYR-515, contracts v0.31.0), or NULL when the server holds no fix. THE SAME COORDINATE PAIR, at the SAME PRECISION, as VehicleState.latitude / VehicleState.longitude (rest-api.md §7.1) and as the live `vehicle_update` frame — read from the same AES-256-GCM-encrypted columns by the same resolver, so the catalog and the snapshot cannot disagree about where a car is. WHY IT IS ON THE CATALOG: the rider's vehicle picker renders a per-row pickup ETA, and it has no other input for a row it is not actively watching — a client holds exactly ONE coordinate (the watched car's, from the single-vehicle WebSocket subscription), and a viewer's per-row /snapshot is 403 by design (MYR-432/449). Without this field the picker can only rank the one car the user already opened. A NULLABLE OBJECT, NOT TWO NULLABLE SCALARS: latitude and longitude form an ATOMIC GROUP (rest-api.md §5.4) and splitting one is itself a contract violation, so nesting makes 'both or neither' structural — there is no way to express the half-state two flat fields would permit. Consumers MUST treat the object as indivisible and MUST NOT carry one axis forward from a previous read. NULL IS THE ONLY 'NO FIX' SPELLING ON THIS SURFACE, and this is a DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from §7.1: VehicleState's columns are NOT NULL, so that surface uses the (0, 0) sentinel described in vehicle-state-schema.md §2.3 and asks consumers to re-interpret it. This surface can express absence, so it does — the server collapses an exact (0, 0) to `null` before emitting, and a consumer will NEVER receive 0,0 here. Do not port a Gulf-of-Guinea guard to this field; do not treat `{latitude: 0, longitude: 0}` as reachable. RBAC: BOTH roles, and the reasoning matters because this is the first P1 field on this resource other than `licensePlate`. A viewer ALREADY receives latitude/longitude at full precision on the streaming path for exactly these vehicles — the viewer mask retains the whole Speed/GPS atomic group, and MYR-435's narrowing deliberately left it — so this is the same value over a different transport to a party already entitled to it, not a new disclosure. The honest caveat: the catalog hands a viewer N positions at once where the socket hands out one per subscription, which is an AGGREGATION difference rather than an entitlement one, since the grant is per-vehicle and a viewer could subscribe to each car in turn. ON COARSENING: considered and deliberately not applied. The platform has no precision convention, and rounding this row while the socket serves the exact value would protect nothing while degrading the short-hop ETA this field exists for; if a future policy coarsens shared positions it must coarsen the stream and this row together. P1 handling binds in full: never logged, never emitted outside the vehicle's party, encrypted at rest. A row exists only because a live accepted grant produced it, so a suspended or revoked grant yields no row and therefore no coordinate. OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: an ABSENT key means a server predating v0.31.0 and MUST be read exactly like null. Delivery: REST-READ-TIME ONLY — a `vehicle_update` frame never carries a `location` object under this name; the live position arrives as the flat VehicleState fields on the socket. So this value is as fresh as the last write to the vehicle row, and a consumer watching a car should prefer the socket's coordinate over this one.

latitude.description: WGS-84 latitude. Named `latitude`/`longitude` rather than RidePlace's `lat`/`lng` to match VehicleState and SavedPlace — both spellings exist on the platform and this surface follows the account/vehicle family. Full precision, matching VehicleState.latitude exactly; see the parent description for why it is not coarsened.

longitude.description: WGS-84 longitude. The other half of an ATOMIC PAIR — see `latitude` and the parent description. A consumer that receives this object receives both axes or neither.

vinLast4.description: Last 4 characters of the vehicle's 17-character VIN. The full VIN is never emitted on the list endpoint — vinLast4 is sufficient for human disambiguation in the catalog UI without exposing the full identifier. Empty string when the VIN is unknown.

status.description: Derived vehicle status snapshot at the time of the last telemetry update. Same enum as VehicleState.status.

chargeLevel.description: Battery state of charge snapshot at the time of the last telemetry update. Same semantics as VehicleState.chargeLevel.

estimatedRange.description: Estimated remaining driving range snapshot at the time of the last telemetry update. Same semantics as VehicleState.estimatedRange.

lastUpdated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent telemetry update applied to this vehicle. Same semantics as VehicleState.lastUpdated. Telemetry emits RFC 3339 UTC strings (e.g., '2026-05-25T17:30:00Z').

role.description: RBAC role the caller holds against this vehicle. v1 only emits 'owner' rows (every vehicle returned is one the caller owns via Vehicle.userId). The 'viewer' value goes live with the vehicle-sharing self-serve track (MYR-184): once a rider redeems an invite code, the vehicles they were granted are merged into their list as 'viewer' rows (the MYR-91 viewer merge), each carrying the sibling `sharePermission` tier.

telemetrySuspendedAt.description: WHEN OWNER-INACTIVITY SUSPENDED THIS VEHICLE'S TELEMETRY STREAMING, or null/absent while streaming is configured normally (MYR-592, contracts v0.38.0). THE POLICY, stated so a consumer renders it truthfully: after five consecutive days without any authenticated activity from the vehicle's OWNER (server-observed; a real app open necessarily produces it), the platform removes the vehicle's fleet-telemetry configuration to stop the per-vehicle streaming cost. Nothing else is touched — the OAuth grant, the virtual key, the vehicle row and every share survive — which is exactly what makes re-connecting seamless (no OAuth, no lock/unlock; those belong to FIRST pairing only). STRICTLY THE OWNER'S ACTIVITY: rider/viewer usage does not defer suspension (explicit client decision), so a viewer may see a suspended car whose owner has been away — the honest rendering for them is the ordinary no-live-telemetry state, never an error. THE OWNER-FACING RENDERING is the contract's point: the owning account's app MUST show a disconnect notice ("Due to inactivity we've stopped streaming Vehicle Telemetry and have disconnected your vehicle") with exactly two offers — RE-CONNECT (POST the reconnect endpoint; streaming resumes, the field returns to null on the next read) and UNLINK COMPLETELY (the existing vehicle teardown). Consumers MUST NOT render a suspended vehicle as broken, in-service, or offline-forever: it is a deliberate, reversible platform action with a timestamp. The instant is when the config was removed — use it for copy ("disconnected 3 days ago"), never for any countdown. A warning push precedes suspension by one day; that is push-side and carries no field here. OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: absent means a pre-v0.38.0 server and MUST be read exactly like null. REST-READ-TIME ONLY — no WebSocket frame carries it (a suspended vehicle emits no frames at all, which is the whole point).

ownerFirstName.description: THE OWNING ACCOUNT'S DISPLAY FIRST NAME (MYR-581, contracts v0.37.0) — who this car belongs to, on every row of the catalog. FIRST NAME ONLY, AND THAT IS THE PLATFORM POLICY RATHER THAN A CHOICE THIS FIELD MAKES: a counterparty learns the minimum needed to recognise a person, so no surname, no email, no phone, no user id — the same P1 first-names-only rule that already governs RideRequest.requesterName, RedeemShareInviteResponse.ownerFirstName and RideMember.firstName (MYR-229). RESOLUTION, exactly, and it is the platform's THREE-SOURCE NAME LADDER walked server-side in order: (1) `User.name` — the Prisma web account's display name, which MYR-581's `PATCH /api/users/me` (the mandatory name prompt) writes; (2) failing that, the APPLE-CONSENT IDENTITY captured at Sign in with Apple, which is the only name an Apple-only account ever supplies and which Apple hands over exactly once; (3) failing that, the GO-NATIVE user row. The first source that yields a name wins, and whatever it yields is REDUCED TO ITS FIRST TOKEN before emission — 'Alex Rivera' emits 'Alex' — so a consumer receives a first name no matter which rung answered and MUST NOT split, trim or re-derive one itself. NOT THE CAR'S NICKNAME: the sibling `name` is the OWNER'S OWN LABEL for the vehicle ('Optimus', 'The Bus') and identifies nobody — two friends' cars can both be called 'Tesla' — so it cannot answer the question a rider actually has, which is WHOSE CAR THIS IS. This field is the only thing on the row that answers it. EMITTED ON EVERY §7.0 ROW UNDER BOTH ROLES, viewer and owner alike, and the owner's own rows are deliberately NOT an exception: the list is one shape and a client renders one row template, so an owner reading their own garage simply sees their own first name where a rider sees their friend's. ABSENT OR NULL MEANS THE OWNER HAS NO CONFIRMED NAME (MYR-583): the ladder came back empty, OR a ladder-resolvable name exists that its owner has never CONFIRMED through MYR-581's mandatory prompt — a legacy or Apple-consent name nobody has answered for is not evidence of who the owner is, so the server withholds it until the owner confirms (the `PATCH /api/users/me` write records the confirmation). It means nothing else: never 'we could not read it', never a fetch failure, never a per-account privacy suppression (there is no such hiding in v1). NOTE THE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from the sibling surfaces named above, which guarantee a non-empty string by falling back to an email local-part or a generic word: THIS FIELD HAS NO SUCH FALLBACK, because a fabricated name here would be an offer to book a ride the server is about to refuse. CONSUMERS MUST NOT FABRICATE ONE EITHER: no 'Owner', no 'A friend', no initial derived from an email address, no borrowing of the vehicle nickname. THAT REFUSAL IS THE CLIENT'S RULE AND IT IS ENFORCED SERVER-SIDE: a vehicle whose owner has no resolvable name IS NOT OFFERABLE FOR RIDE REQUESTS — the create path (`POST /api/ride-requests`) rejects it with 409 `vehicle_unavailable`, the same status and the same code an owner's ride-share pause yields, as documented in the telemetry repo's rest-api.md — so a consumer MUST render such a row as an UNAVAILABILITY, greyed with a reason, in exactly the register it already uses for `rideShareEnabled: false` or a non-null `setupState`, and MUST NOT let a rider fill in a pickup and then surface the rejection as an error. WHY ABSENCE IS TRANSIENT: rung (1) is written by MYR-581's mandatory prompt, which every account now passes through, so this converges to non-null for active accounts — a null marks a dormant owner, not a supported steady state. Classified P1, and this is the first field on this resource that names a PERSON rather than a car: redact it in logs, NEVER place it in a URL or query string, and never emit it outside the vehicle's party (the owner plus the invited viewers of that vehicle) — the same handling the siblings `licensePlate` and `location` already carry, and the reason it is P1 rather than the P0 of its neighbours `role` and `name`. OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: an ABSENT key means a server predating v0.37.0 and MUST be read exactly like null. Delivery: REST-READ-TIME ONLY, exactly like the siblings `role` and `rideShareEnabled` — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries ownerFirstName — so an owner's rename reaches a catalog on its next read of GET /api/vehicles.

hasActiveRide.description: True when this vehicle currently has an OPEN INSTANT ride request — a RideRequest whose status is 'accepted', 'arrived', or 'enroute'. That state list is exactly the one enforced by the per-vehicle one-active-ride partial unique index `uq_go_ride_requests_active_instant_vehicle` (MYR-266), so this flag and the server's accept guard can never disagree: if the flag is true an accept would conflict, and if an accept conflicts the flag is true. Scheduled rides are EXEMPT and never make a vehicle busy — a request with scheduledFor set (DB scheduled_for) is outside the index and outside this flag no matter its status. 'requested' does NOT count either: a pending request the owner has not accepted yet does not make the car busy (several riders may have open requests against the same idle vehicle). OPTIONAL and deliberately tolerant: absence means the server predates this field, NOT that the vehicle is free-and-confirmed. Consumers MUST treat an absent value as 'availability unknown → treat as available' and MUST NEVER render a Busy state from absence. Consumer guidance: riders use true to render a Busy state on the vehicle and to gate new INSTANT requests toward the scheduling flow instead; the one rider who owns the open ride is the exception — their own ride state takes precedence client-side, so they see the vehicle as their active ride, never as Busy. Derivation is REST-read-time only, computed per row when GET /api/vehicles is served; v1 has NO live WebSocket push of this flag to non-party viewers, so a rider's Busy badge only refreshes on the next list fetch. P0 operational state (whether the car is in service right now), not identifying data — same classification as the sibling `status` field.

licensePlate.description: Owner-entered license plate for this vehicle, same value and same semantics as VehicleState.licensePlate. NOT sourced from Tesla — the Fleet API exposes no plate on any endpoint, telemetry field, or proto, so this value exists only because the vehicle's owner typed it: it is set and cleared via `PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/plate` (MYR-286) and persisted server-side. The server NORMALIZES on write — uppercased, leading/trailing whitespace trimmed, at most 10 characters, and restricted to the charset A-Z, 0-9, space, and hyphen; submitting an empty string to that PUT CLEARS the stored plate. List rows therefore only ever carry an already-normalized value, so consumers MUST NOT re-normalize or re-validate before display. OPTIONAL and deliberately tolerant: ABSENT and EMPTY STRING both mean 'no plate set' (an absent field additionally means the server may predate MYR-286) — neither ever means 'this car has a plate we could not read'. Consumers MUST keep their existing `VIN ····xxxx` fallback label (built from the sibling `vinLast4`) for both cases and MUST NEVER render an empty plate in a catalog row — no blank chip, no stray separator. Visibility is deliberately BOTH ROLES: rows returned with `role` = 'owner' AND rows returned to a viewer/rider both carry this field, unlike VehicleState.vin, which MYR-279 gated to the owner role mask. That asymmetry is an intentional product decision, not an oversight — the entire purpose of the plate is that a rider can identify the correct car at pickup, which fails if only the owner can see it. Classified P1 rather than P0 (unlike the sibling `model`/`color`) precisely because of that reach: a plate is externally correlatable to a person via DMV and third-party registry lookups, so it is identifying data — redact it in logs and never emit it outside the vehicle's party (owner plus invited viewers/riders of that vehicle). Delivery: v1 carries NO live WebSocket delta for this field — a vehicle_update frame NEVER contains licensePlate, and a plate edit fires no push. It changes only through the PUT above and reaches clients on the next read of GET /api/vehicles (this envelope) or the REST /snapshot, so a catalog list refreshes the plate on its next fetch.

serviceEstimatedEndAt.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 UTC instant at which this vehicle's CURRENT SERVICE VISIT is estimated to END — same value and same semantics as VehicleState.serviceEstimatedEndAt (MYR-316). Meaningful only while the sibling `status` is 'in_service': owners render it as 'Estimated completion …' beneath the In Service status in the catalog row, and the rider scheduling flow uses it as a FLOOR on when a ride may be booked against this vehicle. SERVER-COMPUTED, never client-supplied, with a fixed SOURCE PRECEDENCE: (1) Tesla's own estimate, `service_data.service_etc` from the Fleet API `GET /api/1/vehicles/{vin}/service_data`, polled on connectivity edges while the vehicle is in service; (2) failing that, the OWNER-ENTERED 'expected back' value, set via `PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/service-window` (MYR-316); (3) null when neither exists. Tesla returns an ALL-NULL service_data body for visits that have no appointment record, so an absent estimate is COMMON AND NORMAL — it is not an error, not a fetch failure, and not a claim that the car is back. CLEARED AUTOMATICALLY when the vehicle leaves 'in_service': a row whose `status` is driving/parked/charging/offline never carries a non-null value, so consumers never need to age this field out themselves. CONSUMER RULES: the rider scheduling picker floors its selectable range at this instant plus a small buffer, and the server likewise REFUSES scheduled ride requests for a time before it; when the field is ABSENT or NULL there is NO BOUND and scheduling stays fully open — consumers MUST NEVER block or gate scheduling on missing data. Delivery: NOT STREAMED. This field is REST-derived and carries no live WebSocket delta — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER contains serviceEstimatedEndAt — so it is SNAPSHOT-ONLY for the Kit merger and refreshes only on the next read of `GET /api/vehicles` (this envelope) or the REST `/snapshot`. Classified P0: operational timing about the car, not identifying data and not user content — the same tier as the sibling `status`.

sharePermission.description: The access the caller holds over this SHARED vehicle (MYR-184), and as of MYR-369 a DERIVED COMPATIBILITY VALUE rather than a stored tier. DERIVATION, exactly: the caller's accepted grant is read, and the row emits 'rides' when that grant's `allowRides` flag is set and 'live' otherwise. 'live_history' IS NEVER EMITTED — the tier is retired and a legacy grant created at that preset derives 'live' (see vehicle-sharing.schema.json SharePermission). A SUSPENDED GRANT PRODUCES NO ROW AT ALL: suspension removes the vehicle from the viewer's access set, so the vehicle is absent from this list entirely rather than present with some reduced value — consumers must not look for a 'suspended' marker here, there is none by construction. PRESENT ONLY ON VIEWER ROWS: emitted if and only if the sibling `role` is 'viewer', and always OMITTED on `role` = 'owner' rows, where it would be meaningless (an owner is not on a tier — they hold everything). OPTIONAL and additive, so it can never break an existing decoder: absence means either 'this is an owner row' or 'the server predates MYR-184', and consumers MUST treat an absent value on a viewer row as the LOWEST access ('live') rather than as full access — never fail open. Consumer guidance: gate the ride-request affordance on `== 'rides'`. The pre-MYR-369 instruction to compare with a cumulative >= over live < live_history < rides is OBSOLETE — the underlying model is now a set of independent editable flags, not a total order — though a >= comparison over the two values that are actually emitted happens to give the same answer, so an un-updated client stays correct. The history/drives surfaces are OWNER-ONLY as of MYR-369 and no value of this field opens them. This is a UI-AFFORDANCE HINT ONLY: the server independently enforces every gate, so a client that ignores this field cannot escalate, and a client MUST NOT infer that a hidden affordance is unenforced. NO LONGER FIXED for the life of the grant: PATCH /api/invites/{inviteId} lets the owner flip `allowRides` in place, so this value can change between two reads of the same grant without the row appearing or disappearing. Delivery: REST-read-time only, exactly like the sibling `role` — there is NO WebSocket delta for it (a vehicle_update frame NEVER carries sharePermission), so it refreshes on the next GET /api/vehicles, which is also the only moment a viewer learns of a suspension or a capability change. Also carried on the RedeemShareInviteResponse.vehicles rows so the rider's join screen has it immediately. P0 — an authorization value describing the caller's relationship to the car, not identifying data (same classification as the sibling `role`).

rideShareEnabled.description: Whether this vehicle's OWNER currently accepts ride requests against it (MYR-342). TRUE is the ordinary state and the state every vehicle starts in. FALSE means THE OWNER HAS PAUSED RIDE REQUESTS FOR THIS VEHICLE: the car itself may be perfectly healthy — online, parked, idle, not in service — but its owner has withdrawn it from ride-hailing, so the server refuses new ride requests against it (409 `vehicle_unavailable`, message 'Ride sharing is paused for this vehicle') and refuses to accept requests that are already outstanding. OPTIONAL AND DELIBERATELY TOLERANT: ABSENT means the server predates contracts v0.20.0 and MUST be read as ENABLED (true). Absence NEVER means paused — consumers MUST NOT render a paused state, MUST NOT hide the ride-request affordance, and MUST NOT fail closed on a missing key. OWNER INTENT, NOT VEHICLE STATE: unlike the sibling `status` ('in_service') or `hasActiveRide`, nothing the car does sets or clears this, and nothing clears it on a timer — it changes only when the owner changes it, via `PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/ride-share` (owner-only; a viewer holding any share tier gets 403 `vehicle_not_owned`). That is exactly why the server applies the pause to SCHEDULED rides as well as instant ones, a DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the in-service/offline exemption that rest-api.md §7.8 grants reservations: a service visit ends on its own, an owner's pause is open-ended, so exempting reservations would let a rider book a car its owner has withdrawn indefinitely. VISIBLE TO VIEWERS: emitted on `role` = 'viewer' rows as well as owner rows, by deliberate product decision and for the same reason as `licensePlate` and `hasActiveRide` — a rider must be able to see that the car shared with them is not taking requests, rather than discovering it from a 409 after filling in a pickup. CONSUMER GUIDANCE: owners render it as the current position of the ride-sharing toggle (this field IS that position); viewers render the vehicle as paused/unavailable and suppress the request affordance — but MUST NOT treat a hidden affordance as the enforcement, because the server independently refuses both create and accept. Delivery: REST-READ-TIME ONLY, exactly like the siblings `role` and `sharePermission` — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries rideShareEnabled — so a catalog refreshes it on the next read of GET /api/vehicles or the REST /snapshot (which carries the same field, VehicleState.rideShareEnabled), or from the echo the PUT above returns. P0: an owner's availability switch on their own car — operational state, not identifying data and not user content, the same tier as the siblings `status` and `hasActiveRide`.

teslaAccessType.description: WHETHER THE ACCOUNT THAT LINKED THIS CAR OWNS IT ON TESLA'S SIDE OR MERELY DRIVES IT (MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0) — the `access_type` Tesla's Fleet API reports for the vehicle under the account that linked it, narrowed to the two values the platform acts on. 'owner' — the linker is the vehicle's Tesla owner. This is the ordinary case, and the ONLY case that existed before v0.39.0, when a non-owner vehicle was silently skipped at provisioning time (`owner_vehicle_skipped reason=not_owner`) and the person who linked it simply never saw their car appear. 'driver' — the linker holds DRIVER access on somebody else's Tesla account (a family car, a partner's car), which Tesla grants without transferring ownership. WHAT IT IS FOR, and it is two distinct jobs, NEITHER of which `setupState` can do: (1) COPY — Settings vehicle rows, the review card and the picker say 'You drive this car' on a driver row, so a person with a mixed garage can tell at a glance which cars are actually theirs; (2) THE ACKNOWLEDGMENT SHEET — a driver-linked car is provisioned but NOTHING is pushed to it until the linker explicitly acknowledges that the owner approved adding it (`POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/acknowledge-owner-approval`, body vehicle-setup-completion.schema.json#/$defs/AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest, canonical copy shipped alongside these schemas), and THIS FIELD is what lets a client offer that sheet again even AFTER `setupState` has cleared to null. Read the two together: `setupState.state` = 'awaiting_owner_acknowledgment' is the TRANSIENT gate that clears the moment the acknowledgment is recorded; this field is the PERMANENT fact about the relationship and does not change for the life of the row. IT IS NOT A PERMISSION AND NOT A ROLE: the sibling `role` says whether the CALLER owns the platform's vehicle record ('owner') or was shared into it ('viewer'), which is a MyRoboTaxi-side fact; this field says what TESLA thinks of the linking account, which is an upstream fact. A row may perfectly well be role='owner' and teslaAccessType='driver' — that is exactly the case this field exists for. OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: an ABSENT key means a server predating v0.39.0 and MUST be read as 'owner' — absence is a positive 'owner' by construction, not 'unknown', because such a server provisioned owner-access cars only. An UNRECOGNISED value MUST be read as 'owner' too: a client MUST NOT paint driver copy, and MUST NOT gate anything, on a value it does not know. RBAC: BOTH roles — a viewer sees it on a shared row exactly as the owner sees it on their own. Delivery: REST-READ-TIME ONLY, exactly like the siblings `role`, `rideShareEnabled` and `setupState` — a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries teslaAccessType — so it refreshes on the next read of GET /api/vehicles (this envelope) or the REST /snapshot. Classified P0: an operational fact about how the car reached the platform, the same tier as the siblings `role` and `setupState`, carrying no VIN, no coordinate, no credential and no user content.

setupState.description: What is still standing between this vehicle and live telemetry, or NULL when there is nothing to say (MYR-491, contracts v0.24.0) — THE SAME OBJECT, THE SAME MEMBERS AND THE SAME SEMANTICS as VehicleState.setupState (rest-api.md §7.1), produced by the SAME server-side derivation over the same inputs, so the catalog row and the snapshot for one vehicle can never disagree. Read that field's description for the full contract, including the honesty rules the server guarantees and the reason `null` must not be rendered as 'ready'. CARRIED ON THE CATALOG AS WELL AS THE SNAPSHOT ON PURPOSE, and for a different consumer: MYR-437's rider-side picker reads list rows, and today it renders a never-streamed shared car as permanently 'offline' — a car whose status column is still the write-once schema default. This field is what lets the picker say 'still being set up' instead, and grey the row with a reason, without fetching a snapshot per vehicle. (Contrast `hasActiveRide`, which is list-only; setupState is on both surfaces because both surfaces have a consumer.) OPTIONAL AND TOLERANT: an ABSENT key means a server predating v0.24.0 and MUST be read exactly like null. RBAC: BOTH roles — P0 operational state about the car, the same tier as the sibling `status` it qualifies. Delivery: REST-READ-TIME ONLY; a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries it.

state.description: Which setup condition holds. Identical member set and identical meanings to VehicleState.setupState.state — see that field for the per-member owner action. The member set gained `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment` in MYR-599 / contracts v0.39.0 — a car linked by someone who holds DRIVER access on Tesla's side, which the platform will not configure until that person acknowledges the owner approved it; it SORTS FIRST, before `owner_access_required` / `awaiting_virtual_key` / `configuring` / `token_failed`, and the sibling `teslaAccessType` carries the lasting half of that fact. The member set gained `owner_access_required` in MYR-599 / contracts v0.40.0 — Tesla REFUSED to create this car's fleet-telemetry config because the linking account holds DRIVER access and Tesla's Fleet API lets ONLY the vehicle's OWNER account create one; `since` is when that refusal was observed. It SORTS AFTER `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment`, the only state it can follow, and BEFORE `awaiting_virtual_key` / `configuring` / `token_failed`. THE LINKER CANNOT FIX IT BY RECONNECTING: copy MUST NOT say 'reconnect Tesla' (that is `token_failed`'s action) — the honest action is for the car's Tesla OWNER to add the car under their own account and share it with the driver. Consumers MUST treat an unrecognised value as 'setup is incomplete, reason unknown' and MUST NOT fail the decode.

since.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant at which the evidence behind `state` was recorded. Identical to VehicleState.setupState.since: data for the copy, never zero, never in the future.
